draft.title: The end of French rule
card: France ruled Vietnam as part of French Indochina. After the Second World War, the Viet Minh, a communist-led independence movement under Ho Chi Minh, fought to end that rule.
In 1954 the Viet Minh defeated the French army at Dien Bien Phu. This defeat convinced France to end the war and leave Vietnam.
The Geneva Accords of 1954 split Vietnam in two along a line near the 17th parallel. The split was meant to be temporary.
Elections were meant to reunite the country in 1956. They were never held, so the division stayed in place.
draft.remember: Defeat at Dien Bien Phu ended French rule. The Geneva Accords then split Vietnam, and promised elections never happened.

a.q: What was the main result of the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu in 1954?
opts: France gave up the war and agreed to leave Vietnam
Vietnam was reunited under one government at once
The United States sent combat troops to Vietnam
The Viet Minh agreed to stop fighting for independence
a.why: The defeat convinced France to end the war, which led to the Geneva Accords. Vietnam was not reunited at once: it was split in two.
a.clue: Think about what the loss meant for France's will to keep fighting.

b.q: Why did Vietnam remain divided after the Geneva Accords, even though the split was meant to be temporary?
opts: The elections meant to reunite it were never held
The Viet Minh refused to accept the Geneva Accords
France won back control of the south in 1956
The line at the 17th parallel was made permanent
b.why: The Accords set the split as temporary, until elections to reunite the country. Those elections were never held, so the division stayed. The line was not written as permanent, which makes that option tempting but wrong.
b.clue: Look at what was supposed to end the split.

a.best: France gave up the war and agreed to leave Vietnam

b.best: The elections meant to reunite it were never held

check.summary: No problems found. The facts on Dien Bien Phu, the Geneva Accords, the 17th parallel and the 1956 elections are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer.
